analyst_view.overall: Spurs (11th, 12 pts) host Ipswich (14th, 11 pts) after a 1-0 defeat at Leeds ended a run of three straight wins. Mathys Tel, hurt by a heavy challenge at Leeds, is now described as a major doubt and unlikely to play, which matches the numbers (they already take his goal share off); Xavi Simons and Odobert are long-term out. The good news for Roberto De Zerbi is that Savio, Lucas Bergvall, Mykhailo Mudryk and James Maddison are all reported close to returning, though probably from the bench for most of them. Ipswich, under Gary O'Neil, are winless in four (two draws, two defeats, conceding in all of them); I found no Ipswich team news after a real search, so their side of this view rests on form. Referee Robert Jones (4.3 cards a game) is already in the numbers.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, already taking about 6% off Spurs for Tel, who is still unlikely to play. What they can't see is Spurs getting creators back: Maddison (no league minutes since the Chelsea game) and Savio are both in line to return, at least off the bench, against an Ipswich side that has conceded in every game of a four-match winless run. A small nudge up: about 3.2.

corners.text: The numbers say 10.7 corners, with Spurs' heavy recent corner count (48 in six) and Ipswich's low one (14 in six) already in the momentum adjustment. Returning wingers like Savio and Mudryk fit Spurs' wide play but are more likely to come off the bench, so nothing pushes this further: about 10.7.

cards.text: The numbers say 5.0 cards, already adding about 12% for referee Robert Jones (4.3 cards a game) and Ipswich's slightly higher card count lately. There's no derby edge, no suspension story and nothing new on discipline from either camp, so I stay at 5.0.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots, already adding about 15% to Spurs for their 104 shots in the last six games. Maddison and Savio returning would add quality more than extra volume, and the numbers have already pushed Spurs' shot count high, so I keep 28.7.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 8.7 shots on target. Maddison's shooting from distance and Savio's chance creation, both expected back in the squad, should turn a few more Spurs efforts on target than the side that played without them before the break: about 9.0.
